metadata.description: RepoWise Evaluation Dataset - 60 repository-level Q&A questions

categories.METADATA: Statistics, file counts, contributor counts, language breakdown
categories.SEMANTIC: Implementation details, how code works, function/class explanations
categories.STRUCTURAL: Dependencies, class hierarchies, imports, code relationships
categories.HISTORICAL: Commit history, contributors, who changed what, when
categories.HYBRID: Questions requiring both vector and graph retrieval

routing_legend.GRAPH: Expected to route to Neo4j knowledge graph
routing_legend.VECTOR: Expected to route to ChromaDB vector search
routing_legend.HYBRID: Expected to use both retrieval mechanisms

questions.question: How many files are in the requests repository?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should return a specific file count from the repository
questions.evaluation_criteria: Answer must include a specific number; vague answers are INCORRECT

questions.question: Who are the top 5 contributors to the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should list contributor names with commit counts
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list at least 3 named contributors; generic answers are PARTIAL

questions.question: What programming languages are used in the requests repository?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Primarily Python, with some configuration/documentation files
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention Python as primary; bonus for RST, YAML, etc.

questions.question: How many total commits does the requests repository have?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should return a specific commit count
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must provide a number; answer should be consistent with GitHub data

questions.question: Which files have been modified the most in the requests repository?
questions.ground_truth_hint: sessions.py, models.py, adapters.py are typically hot spots
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific file names; vague answers are INCORRECT

questions.question: How many Python files are in the Flask repository?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should return a specific count of .py files
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must include a specific number

questions.question: Who has made the most contributions to the Flask project?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should name the top contributor with commit count
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name at least one specific contributor

questions.question: What is the total number of lines added and deleted in the last 50 commits of Flask?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should return addition and deletion counts
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must provide two numbers (additions and deletions)

questions.question: How many classes are defined in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should count all class definitions across files
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must provide a specific number; acceptable range is Â±5

questions.question: What are the hot spot files in the Flask repository (most frequently modified)?
questions.ground_truth_hint: app.py, helpers.py are typically frequently modified
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific file names with modification counts

questions.question: How does the Session class handle cookies?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Session uses RequestsCookieJar, merges cookies per request
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must explain the cookie merging/persistence mechanism; generic HTTP answers are PARTIAL

questions.question: What does the PreparedRequest class do in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: PreparedRequest is a mutable prepared version of a Request, ready to be sent
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must explain the preparation/serialization role; must mention it's separate from Request

questions.question: How does retry logic work in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Uses HTTPAdapter with Retry from urllib3, configurable max_retries
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention HTTPAdapter and/or urllib3 Retry; must explain how to configure it

questions.question: Explain how authentication works in the requests library.
questions.ground_truth_hint: Auth classes implement __call__, Session applies auth to PreparedRequest
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention at least one auth method (BasicAuth, BearerToken, etc.)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the hooks system in requests?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Hooks allow event-driven callbacks, e.g., response hook dispatched after each response
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must explain event-driven/callback nature; must give a concrete example

questions.question: How does Flask's application context work?
questions.ground_truth_hint: AppContext pushed/popped, provides g and current_app proxies
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must explain context stack; must mention current_app or g

questions.question: What is the difference between before_request and before_first_request in Flask?
questions.ground_truth_hint: before_request runs before every request, before_first_request only before the first
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must clearly distinguish between the two decorators

questions.question: How does Flask handle error handling and custom error pages?
questions.ground_truth_hint: errorhandler decorator registers handlers for HTTP error codes
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention errorhandler decorator; example of 404/500 handling is CORRECT

questions.question: Explain how Blueprints work in Flask.
questions.ground_truth_hint: Blueprints allow modular app structure, registered on app with url_prefix
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must explain modular routing; must mention registration on app

questions.question: How does streaming work in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: stream=True parameter, iter_content() and iter_lines() methods
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention stream=True; must mention iter_content or iter_lines

questions.question: What is Flask's request context and how is it different from the application context?
questions.ground_truth_hint: RequestContext has request and session proxies; AppContext has current_app and g
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must distinguish both contexts clearly with their respective proxies

questions.question: How does the requests library handle SSL/TLS certificate verification?
questions.ground_truth_hint: verify parameter accepts True/False or path to CA bundle
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention verify parameter; must explain True/False/path options

questions.question: How does Flask's url_for function work?
questions.ground_truth_hint: url_for generates URLs from endpoint names (reverse URL building). Takes endpoint name as first arg, accepts _anchor, _method, _scheme, _external params. Requires active request or app context. Raises BuildError if endpoint not found.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must explain reverse URL building from endpoint name

questions.question: What is the role of the adapters in the requests architecture?
questions.ground_truth_hint: HTTPAdapter handles connection pooling via urllib3, mounted on Session
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention HTTPAdapter and connection pooling

questions.question: How does Flask's test client work?
questions.ground_truth_hint: app.test_client() creates a FlaskClient with full request simulation
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention test_client(); must explain request simulation

questions.question: What files depend on sessions.py in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: api.py, __init__.py import from sessions.py
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific files; must not list files that don't import from sessions.py

questions.question: What classes does models.py define in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Response, Request, PreparedRequest, and others
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific class names from models.py

questions.question: What external libraries does the requests library import?
questions.ground_truth_hint: urllib3, chardet/charset_normalizer, certifi, idna are key dependencies
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list at least 3 specific external libraries

questions.question: How is the requests library structured? Give me an overview of its modules.
questions.ground_truth_hint: api.py, sessions.py, models.py, adapters.py, auth.py, exceptions.py, utils.py
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention at least 5 core modules with brief descriptions

questions.question: What files import from flask/app.py?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Files importing from app.py include: blueprints.py, cli.py, testing.py, sessions.py, sansio/blueprints.py
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific files; vague answers are INCORRECT

questions.question: What functions are defined in flask/helpers.py?
questions.ground_truth_hint: url_for, flash, get_flashed_messages, send_file, send_from_directory
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific function names from helpers.py

questions.question: What is the class hierarchy in the Flask application object?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Flask inherits from Scaffold; Blueprint also inherits from Scaffold
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention the inheritance chain correctly

questions.question: What functions are exported from the requests package's __init__.py?
questions.ground_truth_hint: get, post, put, delete, head, options, patch, request, Session are exported
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list the main HTTP method functions

questions.question: What does auth.py define and what does it depend on?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Defines AuthBase, HTTPBasicAuth, HTTPDigestAuth; depends on models and utils
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must identify both the classes defined and the dependencies

questions.question: How are the Flask modules organized and what does each one do?
questions.ground_truth_hint: app.py (Flask class), blueprints.py, ctx.py, globals.py, helpers.py, routing.py
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention at least 4 modules with correct descriptions

questions.question: What exceptions are defined in the requests library and in which file?
questions.ground_truth_hint: exceptions.py defines RequestException, ConnectionError, Timeout, HTTPError etc.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name the file and at least 3 specific exception classes

questions.question: What does ctx.py define and what does it import?
questions.ground_truth_hint: ctx.py defines AppContext and _AppCtxGlobals (classes); RequestContext was deprecated in Flask 3.2 and merged into AppContext. Also defines functions: after_this_request, copy_current_request_context, has_app_context, has_request_context
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must correctly identify AppContext and _AppCtxGlobals as the main classes defined. RequestContext is deprecated/removed - should NOT be required. Mentioning at least 2 functions like has_app_context, has_request_context is a bonus.

questions.question: Who last modified sessions.py in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: m0d3v last modified sessions.py on 2026-02-13
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name a specific contributor; must be consistent with actual git history

questions.question: What changes were made to the requests library in its most recent commits?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should summarize recent commit messages and changed files
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must reference specific files or changes; generic answers are PARTIAL

questions.question: Which contributor has made the most changes to models.py?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Nate Prewitt has made the most changes to models.py (19 commits), followed by Kenneth Reitz (8 commits)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name a specific contributor

questions.question: How has the requests library evolved over its recent commits? What major changes were made?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should synthesize commit messages to identify major feature/fix trends
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must reference actual commit messages or file changes; speculation is INCORRECT

questions.question: Who are the top contributors to the Flask project and how many commits do they have?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should list contributors with commit counts
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list at least 3 contributors with commit counts

questions.question: What files were changed in the most recent commits to the Flask repository?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Most recent Flask commits changed: helpers.py, ctx.py, app.py, CHANGES.rst, docs files
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific file names; generic answers are INCORRECT

questions.question: What commit added SSL verification support to the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should reference specific commit or acknowledge limitation if not in indexed history
questions.evaluation_criteria: Honest 'not found in indexed data' is CORRECT; hallucination is INCORRECT

questions.question: Which files have been most actively modified in the last 20 commits to Flask?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should return files sorted by modification frequency in recent commits
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific files with counts

questions.question: Show me the commit history for utils.py in the requests library.
questions.ground_truth_hint: Recent commits: 4791422 by Nate Prewitt, f8bec2f by Nate Prewitt, 5b4b64c by Arthur Woimbee
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list specific commits; must include author names or messages

questions.question: What percentage of commits to Flask were made by the top contributor?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should calculate percentage based on indexed commit data
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must provide a calculated percentage; must name the contributor

questions.question: What changes were made to exceptions.py over time in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: exceptions.py history: f8bec2f by Nate Prewitt (Fix CI), 3ff3ff2 by Thomas Dehghani (Fix JSONDecodeError), d63e94f by Nate Prewitt (Move to src)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must reference actual commits; fabricated history is INCORRECT

questions.question: Who contributed the most code (lines added) to the Flask project?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should calculate based on additions in tracked commits
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name specific contributor; must reference line counts

questions.question: Who wrote the Session class and how does it work?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should combine: who authored sessions.py (graph) + how Session works (vector)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must answer BOTH parts: author/contributor AND functional explanation

questions.question: Which files depend on models.py and what are the key classes in it?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Dependencies (graph) + class explanations (vector)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must list dependent files AND explain at least 2 classes

questions.question: What recently changed in app.py and what does the Flask class do?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Recent commits to app.py (graph) + Flask class explanation (vector)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must include both recent change info AND functional description

questions.question: Give me a complete overview of adapters.py: its structure, what it does, and who maintains it.
questions.ground_truth_hint: Structure/classes (graph) + functionality (vector) + contributor history (graph)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must cover all three aspects: structure, functionality, and contribution info

questions.question: Which contributor most recently modified the routing logic in Flask and how does that routing work?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Recent commits to routing.py (graph) + routing mechanism explanation (vector)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name a contributor AND explain the routing mechanism

questions.question: What is the most complex file in the requests library and what does it do?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Complexity can be measured by class/function count (graph) + explanation (vector)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must justify 'most complex' with some metric AND explain what it does

questions.question: What happens when you send a request to an invalid URL in the requests library?
questions.ground_truth_hint: MissingSchema or InvalidSchema exception raised
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention specific exception classes; generic 'error' answers are PARTIAL

questions.question: How does Flask handle circular imports?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Flask uses lazy imports and proxy objects (LocalProxy) to avoid circular imports
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must mention LocalProxy or lazy loading pattern

questions.question: Does the requests library have any circular import dependencies?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Should analyze import graph for cycles
questions.evaluation_criteria: Honest analysis is CORRECT; confident wrong answer is INCORRECT

questions.question: How many functions are in helpers.py, when was it last modified, and who modified it?
questions.ground_truth_hint: Function count (graph) + last commit info (graph)
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must provide function count AND commit/author info

questions.question: What functions are defined in flask/globals.py, when was it last changed, and why do they use LocalProxy?
questions.ground_truth_hint: globals.py defines current_app, request, session, g as LocalProxy objects; last commit from graph
questions.evaluation_criteria: Must name the proxy objects AND explain why LocalProxy is used (thread safety / context isolation)
